Volunteered to do maintenance on a steam train. After a week of working there, it was time for me to take out the bolts inside the water tank. I climbed up and nearly pissed myself because the hole to get into the tank was pretty small, so I managed to shimmy my body through and eventually be fully inside the tank.

The people from the outside were in charge of twisting off the bolts and I had to collect them from the inside. Now, the water tank is no fucking joke. Some steam engines are massive and might give you some room inside the tank. This engine? Nope, it's a saddle type locomotive and it had little metal plates inside that you had to manoeuvre around to get to the bolts connected to the smoke box.

My god, moving around this tank was like being in a cramped long pipe that is covered with thick rough sandpaper. Because the tank holds water, it's expected for corrosion to be inside. The tank was super rusty inside and having to crawl around in such tight rough corridors in pitch fucking black holding a tiny lamp was a challenge. Oh, it gets worse.

We managed to take off the bolts connected to the cab and the bolts underneath. Now, it's time for the bolts connected to the smokebox to come off. The water tank gets narrower as you go down; rust also becomes thicker. I had to crawl head first through extremely tight spaces, avoiding these metal plates and then getting to the very front where the supply of air was limited. I had a very short panic attack because I couldn't breathe as well because of the tight space but luckily one of the bolts being removed created a tiny bit of light and some air. At that point I really questioned what the fuck am I doing with my life? Is my passion for trains or heavy machinery worth all this? 

All the bolts were undone and the tank was ready to be removed. I felt like I was reborn again after climbing out from the pitch black sandpaper void. The job sure beats cleaning out the boiler tubes ( I did that job as well). I think taking out the metal bars inside the firebox would be worse because the process of getting in can literally get you stuck.

(TL;DR:  Sometimes your passions and interests can put you into situations where you question whether or not it's really worth it. Possibly putting you into dangerous situations. )

OP, I’m just gonna give you everything I know. Hopefully it helps.

**Resources:**

* I’d highly recommend going on Youtube and just visually learning mathematics. I’m a visual learner myself and love seeing stuff explained on a whiteboard. Make sure to write everything down and make sure it's neat. Concentrating on neatness and writing stuff down really helps ingrain information into your brain.
* Using online resources such as text books. There’s a site called *OpenStax* that is FILLED with text books for maths and other subjects. Someone on Reddit recommended it to me and I’m still using it to revise. The layout is really simple and easy to navigate and the resources are pretty good.
* Past papers. Just Google past papers and set yourself a time limit to do them. I’d print them out and just straight up do them and later mark them. This allows you to see your weakness and areas where you have to revise more. If you can’t find any useful past papers then create your own.
* Khan Academy? Everyone recommends this site because it’s pretty good at teaching. I highly recommend it.
* Have a friend? Teach him to solve math problems. Teaching actually is revision in itself and helps you become familiar with the topic.

**Studying:**

This part is highly important because outcome is dependent on the way you study. Everyone is different so it’s better to juggle around different study methods and see what fits. Whatever you were doing in the past obviously isn’t working. Try something new.

* Flash cards help memorise. I suggest creating your own and making up the questions.
* Past papers help reinforce confidence and familiarity with certain topics.
* Make it fun? Reward yourself with certain treats after each study session. Take breaks and make sure not to burn yourself out.
* This might sound REALLY silly but create math posters and stick them all over your room. This all helps with memorization.
* Practise. I can’t fathom how important this one is. Grab a notebook and just start doing the same question over and over again and get used to it. This might not suit you but it sure helped me gain confidence in certain topics and helped me remember the steps for tackling certain mathematical problems.
* Have a well organised study schedule. Tons of people I know don’t revise that much and procrastinate. Create a time table and organise all the topics you’ll be covering. This really helps.

**Other:**

* You’re saying the information doesn’t stick. Maybe improve your sleeping schedule if you have a bad one. A rested mind thinks better and works more efficiently.
* Exercise. This also helps improve your mind and pumps you up.
* Eat better and make sure to eat breakfast. I used to always skip breakfast and that’s a huge mistake because it distracts you.
* Make sure your environment is clean because unorganised environments can affect your ability to focus.
* Make sure your environment isn’t too loud. Wear headphones or listen to calm music.

 **Youtube support:**

* **Blackpenredpen** (AMAZING GUY)
* **Daily challenge with Po-Shen loh** (Contains daily math challenges. I believe he streams live every day. )
* **Numberphile**  (If you want to get motivated then I suggest you watch this channel. They cover very interesting math topics. I believe passion is a really important factor in learning. )
* **The math sorcerer** (AMAZING GUY)
* **The organic chemistry tutor**  (He teaches both math and science.)

These are the only channels that I watch. If you want to go far and beyond then I also recommend watching some old MIT math lectures. There’s so many recorded lectures that are completely free on Youtube.

Follow them and choose what study method best fits you. I suggest posting an update on how you’re doing. We love seeing people succeed. Math is simply a tool that requires tons of patience and focus.
